transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Chloe. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Chloe, I'm calling because my fibre broadband keeps cutting out every single evening around eight o'clock, and it's becoming a major nuisance.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I would be glad to look into those evening disconnections for you today. Before we begin troubleshooting, may I take your full address and your four digit security PIN for account verification?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, it is 42 Highbury Terrace, London, N5 1UP, and the PIN is 6814.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Tariq, that has verified your account details on our Fibre 300 package. Let me open up your connection diagnostics here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. It has been happening for almost a week now, strictly in the evenings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what you are experiencing is that every evening around eight o'clock, all your wireless connectivity drops out completely while the physical hub stays powered on, and it takes several minutes to restore. Have I understood the problem accurately, Tariq?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happens. It just drops dead on all our phones and laptops.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. When the connection drops, do you notice what colour the lights on the front of your router show?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The power light stays solid white, but the internet light blinks orange for a bit before going back to white after about five to ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is very helpful diagnostic information. Do you have any desktop computers or gaming consoles plugged directly into the router via an ethernet cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my home office PC is connected directly with a yellow ethernet cable into port one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And when the wireless drops out at eight in the evening, does that desktop PC lose connection as well, or does it stay online?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now that you mention it, my desktop never dropped connection. It was only the laptops and mobiles on Wi-Fi that got disconnected. It's honestly driving me up the wall, I missed an important international work meeting last night because of this!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you open a web browser on your phone or laptop right now and tell me if you can reach the hub management page at 192.168.1.1?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I have the router dashboard open on my tablet right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First of all Tariq, missing an important international work meeting is awful, and I am truly sorry you had to deal with that stress. We are going to get this Wi-Fi stability sorted out properly so it does not interrupt your work again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, Chloe. I really appreciate that. It was so stressful explaining to my team why I dropped off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at your hub telemetry on my system, your fibre optic link to the street cabinet has zero line drops over the past thirty days, which confirms the optical signal is pristine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that's good to hear, so the wire into the house is fine then.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. On your tablet screen under the wireless settings tab, what does it show for the 5GHz Wi-Fi channel number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me see... it says 5GHz channel is currently set to channel 108.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That explains the whole issue. Channel 108 is a Dynamic Frequency Selection channel, also known as DFS. By telecommunications regulations, when a nearby weather radar or airport radar signal is detected, the router must immediately shut off transmission and monitor the frequency for ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, really? There is an airfield about three miles from our house! Could aircraft radar be knocking out our Wi-Fi every night?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is almost certainly what is happening. The automated radar detection triggers an instant radio mute to prevent interference, which looks like a random Wi-Fi crash to your household devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good grief, I had no idea routers did that. I thought the hub was broken or overheating.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously we cannot alter civilian radar frequencies, but what we can do is switch your 5GHz wireless band off the DFS range and lock it permanently to a clean non-DFS channel such as channel 40.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like a great plan. Will that reduce our speed or range at all?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all. Channel 40 delivers the exact same 300 megabit throughput without being subject to mandatory radar shut-off events.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fantastic. Can you do that from your side or do I need to type it in here?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can push the radio configuration profile directly from my terminal. Bear with me for about a minute while I update the router profile and reboot the wireless card.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Tariq. The configuration push has finished and your hub's 5GHz radio is now locked onto clean channel 40.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Welcome back Chloe. The lights on the hub flickered for a few seconds and now they are all solid white again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the Wi-Fi indicator light still solid white after the radio reboot, and can you see your network name appearing on your phone?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the Wi-Fi light is solid white, and my iPhone just reconnected automatically.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Let us also look at the 2.4GHz band while we are here, because smart home accessories like plugs and thermostats rely on that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, we have three smart plugs in the kitchen and living room for the lamps.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On your tablet dashboard, what does it show for the 2.4GHz channel and channel width?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Under 2.4GHz it says channel auto, currently channel 6, channel width 20/40 MHz coexistence.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Setting 20/40 MHz width on 2.4GHz can sometimes cause packet collisions if nearby neighbours have strong routers. I will lock that to a standard 20 MHz width on channel 1 to give your smart plugs rock solid stability.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. Sometimes the kitchen lamp takes a couple of tries to switch on from the app.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have applied that 2.4GHz adjustment now as well. Are the smart plugs still showing as connected in your smart home app?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check the app on my phone... yes, all three plugs show green dots and responded immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us verify your laptop connectivity and run a proper throughput and latency test in your study.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, walking upstairs into the study now. Laptop is awake and connected to the S-Net Wi-Fi.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could you open a browser on the laptop and navigate to speedtest.net or s-net.com/speedtest?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening speedtest.net now. It has selected the London S-Net testing server.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead and click the go button, and read me the download speed, upload speed, and ping time once it finishes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's running the download gauge now... reaching 312 megabits down. Upload is hitting 52 megabits, and ping is eleven milliseconds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: 312 megabits down and 52 up with eleven milliseconds ping is performing above your advertised 300 megabit tier. That shows the connection is in peak health.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is actually faster than I was seeing before the disconnections started. Very impressive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because channel 40 avoids both DFS radar scanning and neighbour interference, your wireless packets travel without retransmissions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes complete sense. Is there anything else I need to keep an eye on?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also run a quick continuous ping test from your command prompt just to confirm zero packet loss over sixty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, how do I do that on Windows?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Press the Windows key and R on your keyboard, type cmd, hit enter, and in the black window type ping bbc.co.uk -n 10.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Doing that now... ping bbc.co.uk -n 10. It is sending ten packets.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tell me what summary statistics appear at the bottom once all ten reply.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says packets sent ten, received ten, lost zero, zero percent loss. Minimum eleven milliseconds, maximum thirteen milliseconds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Zero percent packet loss and a two millisecond jitter spread is textbook performance for video conferencing calls.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me so much peace of mind for my work presentation tomorrow evening, you have no idea.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have locked these radio channel settings permanently on our network management server, so even if the hub loses power during a power cut, it will boot straight back onto channel 40 and 20 MHz.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is brilliant, so I don't have to worry about it resetting back to the radar channel.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you use the S-Net mobile app on your phone, Tariq?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I downloaded it when we signed up, but haven't used it much.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In that app under the broadband tab, you can view all connected devices in real time and even pause internet access for specific gadgets if needed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh that's handy for when the kids are supposed to be doing homework.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It is very convenient. Are all your household devices, including your tablet, smart TV, and phones, running smoothly right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my wife is streaming a show downstairs right now without any buffering, and both laptops are running perfectly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does that completely resolve the evening Wi-Fi disconnection problem for you today, Tariq?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that completely resolves it and explains why it kept dropping every night. Thank you so much for figuring that out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been an absolute pleasure assisting you today. Is there anything else with your S-Net broadband or TV services I can help you with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that was everything I needed. You've been really wonderful, Chloe.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks again. Have a lovely evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net as your broadband provider. Have a wonderful evening Tariq, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Chloe.
